text: Google Slides is a display tool, not an interactive one—it can’t simulate real interface behavior. The real risk is mistaking polished slides for a living demo, which fails the liveliness and clarity tests. A better alternative is a clickable prototype in Figma or Framer, where users can *feel* the interface’s rhythm. Settle it by building a 3-screen prototype and timing how long it takes a first-time user to complete a core task—if it’s under 30 seconds, the slides are dead weight.

name: Pane
text: Figma prototypes solve the liveliness problem but create a new risk: users mistake a polished mockup for a finished product, hiding real usability flaws. A better alternative is a live-coded demo in Observable or CodePen—users see raw code in action, so they judge the *behavior*, not the polish.
